mechanism: At the European open (08:00 London) bank desks execute customer orders accumulated overnight while liquidity providers are still rebuilding books (spreads wide, depth thin; Ito-Hashimoto 2006 on the intraday activity/spread jump at the European open). Amihud-Mendelson 1987 for equity opens; finding 1: short-horizon EURUSD reversion is real but small, so trade only the largest excursions at the point where the liquidity imbalance is greatest). mechanism: Da, Gurun & Warachka (2014 RFS, 'Frog in the pan'): investors with limited attention underreact to information that arrives continuously in small increments much more than to the same total information arriving as a few discrete jumps, so momentum is concentrated in moves with low information discreteness (ID = sgn(R)*(%neg - %pos)). Intraday FX analogue: a large 4h move built from many small same-sign M15 bars is the footprint of gradual information/order flow (sliced metaorders, slow repricing) that the market has not yet fully absorbed, whereas a move of the same size made by one or two jumps is a discrete event that is priced at once (and partly overshoots - finding 1). Ledger link (disclosed): R021 found that long one-directional M15 runs continue (fading lost -0.54, t -3.1, all 4 years) and R026 showed the continuation disappears when the path contains a large counter-bar, i.e. path composition matters. Hold 4h intraday so the 1.05 round trip is small relative to the move and no funding is paid.

mechanism: Short-horizon reversal is the compensation liquidity providers earn for absorbing transient order imbalances (Grossman-Miller 1988; Nagel 2012; Comerton-Forde, Hendershott, Jones, Moulton & Seasholes 2010: the premium rises when market makers' risk-bearing capacity is low). On days when London or New York is closed for a bank holiday, and in the Dec 24 - Jan 2 window, dealer desks are thinly staffed and order books are shallow, so a given liquidity-demand order moves price further than its information warrants and the transient part should be larger and revert. This conditions on a predictable, exogenous drop in liquidity-provider capacity (calendar), not on the realised price path or volatility: R017/R024/R034 conditioned on vol (edge plateaued at ~+1.0) and R023 on spreads (untestable under the 0.7-pip floor). Ledger link disclosed: the band-fade rules are R017's, with the vol filter replaced by the calendar filter; no R017 slice was used.
